functional_checklist.1_explicit_timeouts: Verified withTimeout (1000ms production / 200ms drill) wraps outbound provider calls; Redis configured with fast connect/command fallback; slow provider cut off in 207ms vs 3000ms stall.
functional_checklist.2_circuit_opens_at_threshold: Verified opossum tripped OPEN immediately upon reaching volumeThreshold=5 with >50% failure rate, emitting structured log event='circuit_opened'.
functional_checklist.3_fast_fallback_under_100ms: 5 consecutive open-circuit requests served in 0ms total (0.0ms/req) using an isolated in-memory async retry queue with zero calls to the dead provider.
functional_checklist.4_backoff_and_jitter_in_logs: Verified retry_attempt logs showing non-uniform jittered exponential delays (attempt 1: 36ms, attempt 2: 68ms) and 0 retries on permanent 401 Unauthorized.
functional_checklist.5_circuit_closes_on_recovery: After resetTimeout, breaker emitted circuit_half_open, succeeded on probe, emitted circuit_closed, and reset Prometheus circuit_breaker_state gauge to 0.

conceptual_answers.product_fallback_ux: For Notification Service (Scenario A), when an external provider circuit opens, POST /notifications/send returns HTTP 202 Accepted with { status: 'queued_fallback', degraded: true, queued_id }, guaranteeing zero lost notifications while transparently signaling async delayed delivery.
conceptual_answers.timeout_resource_math: By Little's Law (L = lambda * W), at 100 req/s with a 20-slot pool, a 5s timeout demands 500 concurrent slots (25x pool exhaustion -> total freeze), whereas a 500ms timeout demands 50 slots and drains 10x faster, keeping healthy routes responsive until the circuit breaker opens.
